A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GMValuator work. All 13 pages in each version, including equations, figures, tables, Algorithm 1, and Appendices A–F, support comparison without material gaps.

before.justification: v5 reports original class-matching, attribute-matching, data-cleaning, and efficiency experiments in Section V, plus statistical testing and sensitivity results in Appendices A–C.

after.justification: v7 retains these original experimental results in Section V and Appendices A–C. Their retention qualifies even though no new experiments are added.

M1.justification: Section IV and Algorithm 1 retain the same product-quantization recall, similarity reranking, MANIQA quality calibration, and contribution aggregation. No method component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same tasks on MNIST, CIFAR-10, CelebA, AFHQ, and FFHQ, including noisy-MNIST cleaning and the training-versus-nontraining comparison. Appendix coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: VAE-TracIn remains the comparator in Tables II and IV, and IF4GAN remains in Figure 5 and Table IV. The GMValuator variants participating in each comparison also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Metrics, models, and evaluation settings are unchanged. Examples include 100 generated samples for class matching, the same top-k values, and 100 noisy training images evaluated using 10,000 generated images for cleaning.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the reranking and distance-metric comparisons, qualitative attribute examples, and Appendix C sensitivity analysis over generated sample sizes 1, 10, 30, and 50. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Appendix A retains the same t-tests and 0.01 significance threshold. Appendix C retains the same ten-run procedure and mean/standard-deviation reporting; no seed or uncertainty-reporting information changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables II–VI and findings illustrated in the figures are unchanged. For example, Table II reports CIFAR-10 accuracy at k=30 of 77.94% for GMValuator (DreamSim) and 6.28% for VAE-TracIn in both versions.

T1.justification: The similarity-based valuation assumption, problem formulation, Equations (1)–(4), and computational-complexity reasoning are unchanged. No formal result, derivation, or proof is added or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same model-agnostic, training-free valuation claim, similarity-matching contribution, quality calibration, and four evaluation criteria.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the CIFAR-10 underfitting explanation, DreamSim performance–efficiency tradeoff, sample-size stability interpretation, and Appendix F applications. No substantive qualification or limitation changes.

D1.justification: Table I hardware information, Algorithm 1, and Appendix E dataset and architecture details remain unchanged. No implementation, hyperparameter, or code/data access information is added or revised.

R1.justification: The same 39 references and related-work discussion appear in both PDFs, including the distinction from LAVA and positioning against influence-based generative-model valuation.

P1.justification: v7 removes UESTC from the affiliation block and renumbers the remaining institutions, but leaves several author superscripts unchanged, including a superscript 5 without a corresponding institution. Scientific prose and section/appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Text and floats reflow: Figure 5 moves from the upper-right to the lower-left portion of page 7, and the conclusion begins on page 7 instead of page 8. Some raster images are re-encoded, while figure content, captions, table structures, and numbering remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The scientific argument, experimental evidence, statistical analyses, and reproducibility information are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. The affiliation and layout edits, including the minor affiliation-numbering defect introduced in v7, do not meaningfully change the paper's overall quality.
